Aleph Skill **v2.8.0** improves numerical modeling, makes draft-to-final workflows more reliable, and expands English and Vietnamese evidence intake. This is the public successor to **v2.6.0** and includes the work previously staged for v2.7.0.

## Highlights

- **More expressive causal models.** A node can start at an explicit `initial_value` while retaining its equilibrium `baseline`. Edges can use `all`, `any`, and `veto` conditions across multiple nodes. The execution trace records whether each edge's gate was open so replay can verify its contribution.
- **Formula 2.2.0 for new numerical workspaces.** The engine supports deviation and log-ratio inputs, timestep-aware stock retention, and divergence diagnostics. Formula 2.0.0 and 2.1.0 remain available for replay. Formula 2.2.0 Monte Carlo runs consolidate low-weight regimes when there are more than 12 branches and account for unresolved sample mass separately.
- **A smoother path from draft to final.** Model repair recognizes common node, edge, intervention, and distribution aliases. Compilation accepts wrapped graph arrays. The compiled model binds the simulation inputs, and `finalize_simulation.py --complete` can advance the workspace status and seal receipts in one operation.
- **More precise validation and bilingual intake.** Quality checks identify frozen downstream states, missing material actors, and discrepancies between Vietnamese narratives and numerical outputs. The inducer accepts wide time-series CSVs and English or Vietnamese conditional claims. Correlations produced by CSV intake require causal review.
- **Offline evaluation and richer domain packs.** Adaptive point forecasts, conformal intervals, and an offline backtest runner support time-ordered evaluation. Economics includes 31 reproducible hindcast fixtures with retrospective data. Estimated publication timestamps are flagged in batch backtest summaries. The six other packs gained mechanism templates and retain experimental maturity. The bundled D Research component is pinned to **3.7.0**.

## Upgrade

Choose the [runtime ZIP](https://github.com/d-init-d/aleph-skill/releases/download/v2.8.0/aleph-skill-runtime-v2.8.0.zip) for normal use or the [full ZIP](https://github.com/d-init-d/aleph-skill/releases/download/v2.8.0/aleph-skill-v2.8.0.zip) for development and local release checks. Python 3.10+ and Node.js 18+ are supported.

Install into a fresh directory. Keep a backup of existing workspaces, retain their declared formula version, and replay or validate them before regenerating version-bound receipts. Workspace schema 2.0.0 is the write default. Schema 2.1.0 remains opt-in.

From the extracted directory, check the environment and test a fresh numerical workspace:

```sh
python3 scripts/preflight.py --json
python3 scripts/quickstart_quant.py \
  --slug aleph-v280-demo --change-point "Example policy change" \
  --out-dir ../aleph-demo-output --offline-provisional
```

## Verify the download

Put the two ZIPs, `distribution-manifest.json`, and `SHA256SUMS.txt` in one directory. Verify the listed digests and the provenance of the archive you plan to install:

```sh
sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS.txt  # macOS alternative: shasum -a 256 -c SHA256SUMS.txt

gh attestation verify aleph-skill-v2.8.0.zip \
  --repo d-init-d/aleph-skill \
  --signer-workflow d-init-d/aleph-skill/.github/workflows/release.yml \
  --source-ref refs/tags/v2.8.0

gh attestation verify aleph-skill-runtime-v2.8.0.zip \
  --repo d-init-d/aleph-skill \
  --signer-workflow d-init-d/aleph-skill/.github/workflows/release.yml \
  --source-ref refs/tags/v2.8.0
```

GitHub's attestation service verifies the source tag and workflow identity. The [release workflow](https://github.com/d-init-d/aleph-skill/actions/workflows/release.yml) records the platform checks, reproducible archive builds, and build provenance. Offline provisional runs carry `limited` assurance. Monte Carlo branch weights are relative frequencies until the calibration gates authorize probabilities.
